name: Taekwondo
energy: Repeated short kicking exchanges inside three 2 min rounds with 1 min rest, so high anaerobic power on a moderate to high aerobic base.
summary: Sparring is fast, repeated kicking on one leg with contact to the body and head, and most injuries hit the foot, knee and ankle. The plan builds single-leg strength and kicking power, hip flexor and adductor strength, ankle and landing control, neck strength, and keeps weight making safe.

evidence.claim: Lower-limb injuries are the most common in high-performance taekwondo, especially foot and knee; contusions lead, then sprains and ligament tears, mostly from direct contact.
evidence.source: Epidemiology of injuries in high-performance taekwondo 2025, Cureus

evidence.claim: Amateur competition injury incidence was about 60 per 1,000 athlete-exposures, with about a third of injuries moderate to severe.
evidence.source: Lystad, Graham & Poulos 2013, Br J Sports Med

evidence.claim: Rapid weight loss of 2-10% in the final days before weigh-in is common in combat sports and has documented health harms.

variants.name: Sparring (kyorugi)
variants.desc: Three 2 min rounds of explosive kicking with contact, footwork and head-kick risk.
variants.note: Your plan includes round-based kicking intervals and neck work; follow the weight-making rules.

variants.name: Poomsae (forms)
variants.desc: No contact; balance, flexibility, kick height and control, plus jumping and spinning kicks in freestyle poomsae.
variants.note: Your plan adds landing control and trunk work and skips the round and kicking intervals. The short neck work stays in.

off.name: Lower strength and jump power
off.focus: Leg strength and vertical power for kicks and footwork.

off.name: Hips, rotation, ankles and neck
off.focus: Kicking-hip strength, rotational power and protection work.

slots.note: Strong hip flexors at end range lift the kick and protect the front of the hip.

off.name: Single-leg control and mobility
off.focus: Standing-leg strength, glutes and active range.

pre.name: Heavy lower and kick power
pre.focus: Max strength then explosive single-leg power.

slots.note: Advanced: contrast with the main lift.

pre.name: Rotation, hips and neck
pre.focus: Fast rotation and the protection modules.

in.name: Competition week strength
in.focus: Hold strength and power in 30 minutes, early in the week.

in.name: Light rotation and protection
in.focus: Short session up to 3 days before competing.

off.name: Aerobic base
off.why: Faster recovery between exchanges, rounds and fights.

pre.name: Round simulation
pre.work: 3 x 2 min rounds of pad or bag work: 2-3 s kick flurry, then 5-8 s bouncing footwork, repeated
pre.rest: 1 min between rounds; 3 sets with 5 min between
pre.why: Copies the World Taekwondo format of three 2 min rounds with 1 min rest (practice for the flurry timing).

pre.name: Repeat sprint kicks
pre.work: 5 x 10 s max roundhouse kicks, like the multiple kick test
pre.rest: 10 s between sets, 3 min between blocks; 2-3 blocks
pre.intensity: Max kick rate with full technique
pre.why: Builds the repeat kicking capacity the kick tests measure.

in.name: Top-up round simulation
in.why: Only in weeks without a competition.

tests.name: Frequency speed of kick test, 10 s
tests.how: Partner holds a pad at trunk height; alternate-leg roundhouse kicks for 10 s, count valid kicks.
tests.note: Men's classes from Santos 2019 (regular, good, excellent). Women: regular 17-20, good 21, excellent 22 or more.

tests.name: Multiple frequency speed of kick test
tests.how: 5 x 10 s kick tests with 10 s rest; total kicks and drop-off from best to worst set.
tests.note: Men (Santos 2019). Women: regular 82-91, good 92-96, excellent 97 or more.

tests.name: Countermovement jump
tests.how: Hands on hips, jump mat or My Jump app, best of 3.
tests.note: Practice bands for men; women about 20% lower.

tests.name: Single-leg hop for distance
tests.how: Hop and stick on each leg, best of 3; record the difference between legs.
tests.note: Over 10-15% is a flag for knee injury risk and kicking imbalance (practice).

tests.name: Y-balance anterior reach
tests.how: Single-leg stance, reach forward along a tape line with the other foot; best of 3 each side.
tests.note: A difference over 4 cm is linked to lower-limb injury in other sports (Plisky 2006).

week: Competition Saturday: heavy lower session Monday or Tuesday.
Rotation and protection session Wednesday at the latest.
Hardest sparring 4-5 days out, technical work only in the last 2 days.
No heavy lower work within 72 h of competing.
Day after competing: easy bike, walk or swim and mobility.
primer: Dynamic warm-up with skipping and footwork
2 x 5 fast kicks each leg on the pad
Neck activation 1 x 10 s each way

lines: Last heavy lower lift 5-7 days before competing.
Gym volume down about 50%, keep the load.
Be at your category weight a week out by eating normally, not by cutting water.
Eat and drink normally after weigh-in; random weigh-ins on the day allow only 5% over.

rules: No dehydration to make weight for any amateur: no saunas, sweat suits, fluid restriction or spitting.
Under 18: no weight cutting at all. Compete at natural weight and move up a category if you grow.
Adults: pick a category close to your normal morning weight and lose any extra slowly over weeks.
If you need to drop more than about 2-3% in the final week, choose the next category up.
Keep sparring sessions to about an hour; longer sessions were linked to more injuries.
Head guard, gum shield and shin and foot guards in all sparring.
Any head knock with symptoms: stop that day and follow return-to-play steps.
